Detailed method

The calculator opens at 400 g flour, 64% hydration, 2.2% salt, and 0.5% yeast. That is 256 g water, 8.8 g salt, and 2 g yeast, 666.8 g of dough. The balls fields open at 20 pieces of 33.34 g. Tie that dough into 20 knots and bake them before the garlic goes on. Oil, garlic, and parsley are extra and are not in the gram total. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Mix Stir 400 g flour, 256 g water, 8.8 g salt, and 2 g instant yeast, then knead for about 6 minutes until smooth. At 64% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  2. Rise Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for 80 to 110 minutes. With 0.5% yeast it should about double.
  3. Knot Divide the 666.8 g dough into 20 pieces of 33.34 g, the weight in the balls fields. Roll each one into a rope about 15 cm long and tie a knot. Tuck the ends under. Cover them.
  4. Proof Leave the knots covered for 20 to 30 minutes, until they look slightly puffy.
  5. Bake Heat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until they are golden and the center of a knot is cooked. They should be baked through before you toss them.
  6. Toss While they are hot, toss them with 30 g of oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, and about 5 g of chopped parsley. About 15 g of grated cheese can go into the same bowl. Oil, garlic, parsley, and cheese are extra and are not in the gram total.
  7. Serve Eat them warm. The garlic stays on the crust instead of baking into the dough.
